name: Violight
_turns: How many turns a game lasts (the arena doc); the turn track at the table's end has a slot for each.
_grid: One character per tile, row 0 = the far side (player 2), last row = player 1's side. From the arena's drawing (the user's choice over their play board, which swaps buttons 3 and 4: buttons 1 and 2 set off the zone diagonally across, 3 and 4 the zone straight across). 16x16, all ground level: the centre spire (2x2, solid), four 2x2 capture zones round it, a button on each corner of them, 14 groups of electric tiles, 6 spawns a side.
_legend: level = height step (0 = lowest). surface picks the look from the palette. solid = nothing stands there (no snap points). outline = a glowing line round each group of those tiles. marker = something on the tile (painted, or a 3D piece with piece: true); decal = painted as well as a piece. zone: capture zone tiles (a frame per 2x2 that takes the colour of the player with more Pokemon in it), each tile painted with its zone's number. buttonN: the button that sets off zone N.
_coords: The thunderbolt coordinates (2d8): 1-8 along the middle 8 columns and rows, the same number on opposite edges, each facing out from its edge (set in close to the edge, clear of the spawn circles).
_numbers: How the button and zone numbers read: "both" = a diagonal fraction N/N, upright top left, upside down bottom right, so either player reads it from their side.
_board: The published board files the map picker uses (from tools/build_board.py; update when a new version is published), then run tools/build_arena_index.py.
_table: Image for the table around the board (placeholder until the arena gets its own).
_textures: Placeholders from tools/draw_placeholders.py, a power station at night: dark riveted steel plates with violet light in the seams, electric panels of dark violet glass with yellow lightning (a glowing yellow outline round each group), the spire's top a discharger of coil rings round a glowing core, its sides and the board's edge steel panels with violet bands.
